disclosures.section: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry
sections: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry
disclosures.summary: Output reductions or ramp delays caused by weak demand, oversupply, or supply chain disruptions can lead to production asset underutilization, increasing per-gigabit manufacturing costs and adversely affecting gross margins due to the fixed nature of many manufacturing costs.
disclosures.content:
Many factors may result in a reduction of our output or a delay in ramping production, which could lead to underutilization of our production assets. These factors may include, among others, a weak demand environment, industry oversupply, inventory surpluses, difficulties in ramping emerging technologies, supply chain disruptions, and delays from equipment suppliers.

A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output. As a result, lower utilization, lower wafer output, and corresponding increases in our per gigabit manufacturing costs could result in higher inventory carrying costs, and have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our gross margins, business, results of operations, or financial condition.

sections: Results of Operations > Revenue by Business Unit
disclosures.summary: In 2024, all four business units saw significant revenue increases: CNBU up 67% on higher bit shipments and DRAM ASPs, MBU up 75% from mobile DRAM and NAND ASPs and shipments, EBU up 27% driven by bit shipments despite lower ASPs, and SBU up 80% from higher ASPs and bit shipments.
disclosures.content:
Changes in revenue for each business unit for 2024 as compared to 2023 were as follows:
• CNBU revenue increased 67% driven by increases in bit shipments and DRAM average selling prices.
• MBU revenue increased 75% primarily due to increases in average selling prices and bit shipments for both mobile DRAM and NAND.
• EBU revenue increased 27% primarily due to increases in bit shipments, partially offset by declines in average selling prices.
• SBU revenue increased 80% primarily due to increases in average selling prices and bit shipments.

• MBU revenue decreased 50% primarily due to declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and decreases in NAND bit shipments.
• EBU revenue decreased 31% primarily due to declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and decreases in bit shipments.
• SBU revenue decreased 44% primarily due to declines in average selling prices for NAND partially offset by increases in bit shipments.

disclosures.topic: Classification and Fair Value Measurement of Investments
disclosures.summary: All short-term and long-term marketable investments were classified as available-for-sale with fair values approximating amortized costs. Level 1 securities are measured using quoted prices in active markets, while Level 2 securities use pricing services validated through supplemental analysis, with no adjustments made to pricing information for the periods ended August 29, 2024, and August 31, 2023.
disclosures.content:
All of our short-term investments and long-term marketable investments were classified as available-for-sale as of the dates noted below. Cash and equivalents and the fair values of our available-for-sale investments, which approximated amortized costs, were as follows: (1)The maturities of long-term marketable investments primarily range from one to five years, except for asset-backed securities which are not due at a single maturity date.

(2)The fair value of Level 1 securities is measured based on quoted prices in active markets for identical assets.

(3)The fair value of Level 2 securities is measured using information obtained from pricing services, which obtain quoted market prices for similar instruments, non-binding market consensus prices that are corroborated by observable market data, or various other methodologies, to determine the appropriate value at the measurement date. We perform supplemental analysis to validate information obtained from these pricing services. No adjustments were made to the fair values indicated by such pricing information as of August 29, 2024 or August 31, 2023.

sources.section: Equity Compensation Plans > Employee Stock Purchase Plan ("ESPP")
sources.original_paragraph: Our ESPP is offered to substantially all employees and permitted eligible employees to purchase shares of our common stock through payroll deductions of up to 15% of their eligible compensation, subject to certain limitations. The purchase price of the shares under the ESPP equals 85% of the lower of the fair market value of our common stock on either the first or last day of each six-month offering period. Compensation expense is calculated as of the beginning of the offering period as the fair value of the employees' purchase rights utilizing the Black-Scholes option valuation model and is recognized over the offering period.
